author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Where words come from, and what they picked up on the way.

entries.explanation: Josef Capek suggested the term for R.U.R.; it comes from a Czech word for forced labour.

factCards.text: Horace Walpole coined serendipity in a letter of 28 January 1754, referring to the Persian tale of the three princes of Serendip.
factCards.sourceTitle: Oxford English Dictionary — serendipity, etymology note

factCards.text: The word robot entered English from Karel Capek's 1920 play R.U.R.; Capek credited his brother Josef with the suggestion, based on the Czech robota, forced labour.
factCards.sourceTitle: Oxford English Dictionary — robot, etymology note

factCards.text: The story that the Earl of Sandwich called for meat between bread so as not to leave the gaming table comes from Pierre-Jean Grosley's 1772 account and cannot be independently confirmed.
factCards.sourceTitle: Pierre-Jean Grosley, A Tour to London (1772)
